reason.aboveFoldPrecision: The solve moved the creases much closer to foldable, but not close enough for the pattern to pass the foldability check. Repair the remaining markers — a vertex with an odd number of creases can never be solved, only fixed — and solve again.
reason.answerCollapsed_one: The solver’s answer would collapse 1 crease to zero length, so it was not applied and nothing moved. Its two ends are probably one vertex; merge them and solve again.
reason.answerCollapsed_other: The solver’s answer would collapse {{count}} creases to zero length, so it was not applied and nothing moved. Their ends are probably single vertices; merge them and solve again.
reason.answerCrossings_one: In the solver’s answer 1 pair of creases would cross with no vertex where they meet, so it was not applied and nothing moved. Add a vertex at that crossing, or move the creases apart, and solve again.
reason.answerCrossings_other: In the solver’s answer {{count}} pairs of creases would cross with no vertex where they meet, so it was not applied and nothing moved. Add a vertex at each crossing, or move the creases apart, and solve again.
reason.answerMovedTooFar: The solver’s answer would move a vertex further than it is allowed to, so it was not applied and nothing moved. An edit is probably far from where the crease actually lies.
reason.answerNoCloser: The solver’s answer brought the angles no closer to foldable, so it was not applied and nothing moved. The topology most likely still needs repair.
reason.answerOffPaper_one: The solver’s answer would push 1 vertex off the edge of the paper, so it was not applied and nothing moved.
reason.answerOffPaper_other: The solver’s answer would push {{count}} vertices off the edge of the paper, so it was not applied and nothing moved.
reason.boundaryBroken: The edge of the paper is not a closed square, so the solve could not start. Repair the boundary and try again.
reason.boundaryWorse: The answer pushed a vertex off the edge of the paper, so it was not applied.
reason.crossingsWorse: The answer left creases crossing with no vertex where they meet, so it was not applied. Add the missing vertices and solve again.
reason.degenerateEdges: A crease has both ends at the same point, so the solve could not start. Delete it, or move one end away, and try again.
reason.degenerateWorse: The answer collapsed a crease to zero length, so it was not applied.
reason.malformedInput: The saved solver data does not match this crease pattern, so the solve could not run.
reason.movedTooFar: Making the pattern exact would move a vertex further than the solver is allowed to, so it was not applied. An edit is probably far from where the crease actually lies.
reason.noImprovement: The solver could not improve on the pattern it was given, so nothing was applied. The topology most likely still needs repair.
reason.oddDegreeWorse: The answer left more vertices with an odd number of creases than it started with, so it was not applied.
reason.stillNotFoldable: The solver’s answer would still break a foldability condition, so it was not applied and nothing moved. That is a property of the answer rather than of the pattern as drawn, so there may be no marker for it; adjust the creases near the last edit and solve again.
reason.timeout: The solve ran out of time. You can take how far it got, or repair more of the pattern and try again.

settings.allowDanglingHelp: A dangling fold is a crease with an end on blank paper — nothing to stop at. On, each crease starts from a reference (the paper’s edge or a crease already made) and runs to a second one only when that adds no more crease than the crease itself. Off, every crease runs from reference to reference, however much extra crease that takes.
settings.autoPlayFoldsHelp: Play a step’s fold as soon as its card is reached. Off, the fold plays when you press Play or Space, and plays back when you press again; the paper still turns over on its own.
settings.emptyNote: Open a crease pattern to adjust how its references are found.
settings.mergeSymmetricHelp: Two folds that mirror each other — the left corner to the centre and the right corner to the centre, say — are shown as one step with an arrow for each, the way a diagram folds them. Off, every fold is a step of its own.
settings.showAuxCreasesHelp: The crease pattern’s auxiliary lines, drawn on the paper at every step in the auxiliary crease style and never folded. Follows Settings ▸ Paper until you change it here.
